relatedModels.description: A family of high-performing text embedding models designed for semantic search, retrieval, and multilingual representation tasks.

relatedModels.name: ColBERT
relatedModels.description: A retrieval architecture using token-level contextual embeddings and late interaction, preserving more fine-grained matching information than single-vector dense retrieval.

relatedModels.name: ColBERTv2
relatedModels.description: An improved ColBERT generation using more efficient token-level representations and residual compression for scalable multi-vector retrieval.

relatedModels.name: DDPM
relatedModels.description: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models established the modern diffusion framework for generative modeling by learning to reverse a gradual noise-adding process.

relatedModels.name: DDIM
relatedModels.description: Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models introduced a faster and more flexible non-Markovian sampling process for diffusion models.

relatedModels.name: Latent Diffusion Models
relatedModels.description: Latent Diffusion Models moved the diffusion process from pixel space into a compressed latent space, substantially reducing computational cost while enabling high-quality conditional generation.

sources.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models

relatedModels.name: Stable Diffusion
relatedModels.description: A landmark open latent diffusion model that made high-quality text-to-image generation accessible on consumer hardware and established a major open generative-model ecosystem.

relatedModels.name: Stable Diffusion XL
relatedModels.description: A major Stable Diffusion generation designed for higher-resolution image synthesis and stronger prompt adherence through architectural and conditioning improvements.

context.tokens: latent image representations + multiple text embeddings

relatedModels.name: DiT
relatedModels.description: Diffusion Transformers replaced the conventional U-Net backbone with a Transformer operating on latent image patches, establishing a major alternative architecture for scalable diffusion models.

relatedModels.name: PixArt-α
relatedModels.description: A Diffusion Transformer-based text-to-image model designed to improve training efficiency while maintaining strong image quality and prompt alignment.

relatedModels.name: PixArt-Σ
relatedModels.description: An improved PixArt generation focused on high-resolution synthesis, stronger text alignment, and improved generation efficiency.

relatedModels.name: Sana
relatedModels.description: An efficient text-to-image generation architecture using linear attention, a deep compression autoencoder, and efficient diffusion-transformer design.

relatedModels.name: Stable Diffusion 3
relatedModels.description: A major Stable Diffusion generation using Multimodal Diffusion Transformer blocks with separate parameter sets for image and language representations and flow matching.

architecture.attention: joint multimodal attention with separate modality-specific weights

relatedModels.name: FLUX.1
relatedModels.description: A 12B-class text-to-image family based on hybrid multimodal and parallel diffusion-transformer blocks trained with flow matching.

relatedModels.name: FLUX.1 [schnell]
relatedModels.description: A fast FLUX variant optimized for local development and personal use through distillation and reduced sampling steps.

training.objective: flow matching + latent adversarial diffusion distillation

relatedModels.name: FLUX.1 Kontext
relatedModels.description: A FLUX generation designed for instruction-based image editing and in-context generation while maintaining character, object, and style consistency across edits.

relatedModels.name: Imagen
relatedModels.description: Google's text-to-image diffusion family combining large language-model text representations with diffusion-based image generation.

relatedModels.name: Imagen 2
relatedModels.description: A later Imagen generation improving image quality, photorealism, composition, and generation capabilities.

relatedModels.name: Imagen 3
relatedModels.description: A major Imagen generation focused on higher visual quality, improved prompt understanding, and stronger text-to-image generation.

relatedModels.name: Imagen 4
relatedModels.description: A newer Imagen generation focused on detailed, high-quality image synthesis and improved prompt adherence.

relatedModels.name: DALL·E
relatedModels.description: An early large-scale text-to-image model demonstrating that autoregressive Transformer modeling could generate images conditioned on natural language.

relatedModels.name: DALL·E 2
relatedModels.description: A major transition in the DALL·E lineage toward diffusion-based image generation with CLIP-based semantic conditioning.

relatedModels.name: DALL·E 3
relatedModels.description: A later DALL·E generation focused on improved prompt following, compositional understanding, and natural-language-controlled image generation.

relatedModels.name: S4
relatedModels.description: Structured State Space Sequence models introduced a scalable formulation of continuous-time state-space models for long-range sequence modeling.

sources.title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces

relatedModels.name: S5
relatedModels.description: Simplified State Space Layers reformulated S4 into a single multi-input multi-output state-space layer while retaining efficient long-range sequence modeling.

sources.title: Simplified State Space Layers for Sequence Modeling

relatedModels.name: Mamba
relatedModels.description: Mamba introduced selective state spaces whose parameters depend on the input, providing content-aware sequence processing without conventional attention and with linear scaling in sequence length.

sources.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

relatedModels.name: Mamba-2
relatedModels.description: Mamba-2 introduced the State Space Duality framework, connecting structured state-space models with attention-like computations and producing a faster simplified selective SSM.

relatedModels.name: Mamba-3
relatedModels.description: A later Mamba research generation exploring improved state-space formulations, complex-valued dynamics, and stronger long-context language modeling.

relatedModels.name: RWKV
relatedModels.description: RWKV combines Transformer-like channel mixing with recurrent time mixing, providing parallelizable training and recurrent inference without conventional quadratic attention.

sources.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era

relatedModels.name: RWKV-5
relatedModels.description: RWKV-5 introduced matrix-valued states and improved recurrent time mixing, providing greater representational capacity while retaining efficient recurrent inference.

relatedModels.name: RWKV-6
relatedModels.description: RWKV-6, also known as Finch, introduced dynamic recurrence mechanisms that make the recurrent state update depend more flexibly on the current input.

relatedModels.name: RWKV-7
relatedModels.description: RWKV-7, codenamed Goose, introduces generalized dynamic state evolution and moves beyond earlier attention/linear-attention formulations.

sources.title: RWKV-7 Goose with Expressive Dynamic State Evolution

relatedModels.name: Hyena
relatedModels.description: Hyena is a subquadratic sequence operator replacing attention with implicitly parameterized long convolutions and data-controlled gating.

relatedModels.name: HyenaDNA
relatedModels.description: A genomic foundation model using Hyena operators to model DNA sequences at single-nucleotide resolution with very long contexts.

relatedModels.name: RetNet
relatedModels.description: Retentive Network replaces standard attention with a retention mechanism that supports parallel training, recurrent inference, and chunkwise recurrent computation.

relatedModels.name: xLSTM
relatedModels.description: Extended Long Short-Term Memory revisits recurrent neural networks with exponential gating and matrix-valued memory, creating a modern recurrent architecture capable of scaling to language-model workloads.

relatedModels.name: Linear Attention
relatedModels.description: A broad class of attention alternatives that restructure attention computation to avoid explicitly materializing the full quadratic token-to-token attention matrix.

relatedModels.name: Gated DeltaNet
relatedModels.description: A gated delta-rule sequence architecture combining linear-attention state updates with selective forgetting and input-dependent memory modification.

relatedModels.name: Titans
relatedModels.description: Titans introduces a neural long-term memory that learns during inference and combines it with short-term attention to model very long contexts.

sources.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time

relatedModels.name: BitNet
relatedModels.description: BitNet explores replacing conventional dense floating-point weights with extremely low-bit representations, targeting substantial reductions in memory, energy, and computation.

relatedModels.name: BitNet b1.58
relatedModels.description: BitNet b1.58 extends the 1-bit idea to ternary weights {-1, 0, +1}, aiming to preserve model capability while dramatically reducing arithmetic and memory requirements.

relatedModels.name: Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts
relatedModels.description: A foundational sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture in which a learned gating network routes each token to a small subset of specialized expert networks, allowing parameter count to grow without proportionally increasing computation per token.

sources.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer

relatedModels.name: Switch Transformer
relatedModels.description: Switch Transformer simplified Mixture-of-Experts routing by sending each token to a single expert, enabling very large parameter counts while maintaining relatively low computational cost per token.

scale.activeParameters: single expert plus shared Transformer components

sources.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity

relatedModels.name: GLaM
relatedModels.description: GLaM is a large sparse language model using Mixture-of-Experts layers to increase total parameter capacity while activating only a fraction of parameters for each token.

sources.title: GLaM: Efficient Scaling of Language Models with Mixture-of-Experts

relatedModels.name: Mixtral
relatedModels.description: Mixtral applies sparse Mixture-of-Experts routing to a modern decoder-only Transformer, with each token routed to a small number of experts while retaining a large total parameter capacity.

relatedModels.name: Mixtral 8x7B
relatedModels.description: An 8-expert sparse decoder-only Transformer in which two experts are selected for each token.

relatedModels.name: Mixtral 8x22B
relatedModels.description: A larger Mixtral generation using eight experts and activating two experts per token to provide substantially higher total model capacity.

relatedModels.name: DBRX
relatedModels.description: DBRX is an open-weight decoder-only language model using a fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts architecture with many smaller experts and top-k routing.

relatedModels.name: DeepSeekMoE
relatedModels.description: DeepSeekMoE introduced fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts, allowing specialized experts to model different knowledge while shared experts capture common knowledge.

sources.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

relatedModels.name: DeepSeek-V2
relatedModels.description: DeepSeek-V2 combines fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts with Multi-head Latent Attention, substantially reducing inference cost while maintaining high total parameter capacity.

relatedModels.name: DeepSeek-V3
relatedModels.description: DeepSeek-V3 is a large-scale MoE language model combining fine-grained routed experts, shared experts, Multi-head Latent Attention, and auxiliary-loss-free load balancing.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: shared + routed experts with dynamic load balancing

relatedModels.name: Jamba
relatedModels.description: Jamba combines Mamba State Space layers, Transformer attention, and Mixture-of-Experts layers in a single architecture, demonstrating a hybrid route beyond pure Transformer designs.

relatedModels.name: Qwen MoE
relatedModels.description: The Qwen family includes sparse Mixture-of-Experts variants designed to increase total model capacity while limiting the number of active parameters for each token.

relatedModels.name: Mixture-of-Depths
relatedModels.description: Mixture-of-Depths dynamically allocates a fixed computation budget by routing only selected tokens through expensive Transformer blocks while allowing others to bypass them.

sources.title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in Transformer-based language models

relatedModels.name: Multi-Head Attention
relatedModels.description: The standard Transformer attention mechanism in which multiple attention heads independently project queries, keys, and values, allowing different heads to model different relationships.

relatedModels.name: Multi-Query Attention
relatedModels.description: Multi-Query Attention shares a single key and value head across all query heads, dramatically reducing KV-cache memory during autoregressive decoding.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: multiple query heads with shared K/V

sources.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need

relatedModels.name: Grouped-Query Attention
relatedModels.description: Grouped-Query Attention divides query heads into groups that share key and value heads, providing a middle ground between the expressive capacity of MHA and the KV-cache efficiency of MQA.

sources.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints

relatedModels.name: Multi-Head Latent Attention
relatedModels.description: Multi-Head Latent Attention compresses key-value representations into a shared low-dimensional latent representation for efficient KV caching while retaining multi-head expressive capacity.

relatedModels.name: Sinusoidal Positional Encoding
relatedModels.description: The original Transformer positional encoding represents token positions using deterministic sine and cosine functions added to token representations.

relatedModels.name: RoPE
relatedModels.description: Rotary Position Embedding injects position information by rotating query and key representations according to their token positions, naturally encoding relative positional relationships.

sources.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding

relatedModels.name: ALiBi
relatedModels.description: ALiBi adds position-dependent linear biases directly to attention scores instead of adding explicit positional embeddings.

relatedModels.name: YaRN
relatedModels.description: YaRN provides an efficient method for extending the context window of RoPE-based Transformer models using frequency-aware interpolation and attention-temperature scaling.

sources.title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models

relatedModels.name: LongRoPE
relatedModels.description: LongRoPE extends RoPE-based context windows through non-uniform positional interpolation and evolutionary search over positional scaling factors.

sources.title: LongRoPE: Extending LLM Context Window Beyond 2 Million Tokens

relatedModels.name: Sliding Window Attention
relatedModels.description: Sliding Window Attention restricts each token's attention to a local neighborhood, reducing attention computation while allowing information to propagate across layers.

relatedModels.name: Longformer
relatedModels.description: Longformer combines local sliding-window attention with selected global attention positions to efficiently process long documents.

relatedModels.name: BigBird
relatedModels.description: BigBird combines local attention, random attention, and global attention to reduce the quadratic complexity of full attention while preserving important long-range interactions.

sources.title: Big Bird: Transformers for Longer Sequences

relatedModels.name: FlashAttention
relatedModels.description: FlashAttention is an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that reduces high-bandwidth-memory reads and writes through tiling and kernel-level optimization without approximating the attention result.

sources.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness

relatedModels.name: FlashAttention-2
relatedModels.description: FlashAttention-2 improves GPU work partitioning and parallelism over FlashAttention, substantially increasing attention throughput while retaining exact attention.

sources.title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning

relatedModels.name: Ring Attention
relatedModels.description: Ring Attention distributes long sequences across multiple devices and circulates key-value blocks around a ring, enabling attention over contexts larger than the memory of a single accelerator.

scale.parameters: does not fundamentally change parameter count

sources.title: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context

relatedModels.name: Native Sparse Attention
relatedModels.organization: DeepSeek / Peking University / University of Washington
relatedModels.description: Native Sparse Attention is a trainable sparse attention mechanism using a hierarchical strategy that combines coarse-grained token compression with fine-grained token selection while co-designing the algorithm with modern hardware.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: compressed global view + selected fine-grained tokens

sources.title: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention

relatedModels.name: Byte Pair Encoding
relatedModels.description: Byte Pair Encoding iteratively merges frequent symbol pairs to construct a vocabulary of subword units. It became one of the dominant tokenization approaches for neural language models.

sources.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

relatedModels.name: WordPiece
relatedModels.description: WordPiece constructs a subword vocabulary using a likelihood-oriented vocabulary selection strategy and became strongly associated with BERT-family models.

relatedModels.name: SentencePiece
relatedModels.description: SentencePiece is a language-independent subword tokenizer framework that learns directly from raw text without requiring pre-tokenized word boundaries.

sources.title: SentencePiece: A simple and language independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer for Neural Text Processing

relatedModels.name: Unigram Language Model Tokenization
relatedModels.description: The Unigram tokenizer treats tokenization as a probabilistic segmentation problem and iteratively removes vocabulary pieces while minimizing corpus likelihood loss.

sources.title: Subword Regularization: Improving Neural Network Translation Models with Multiple Subword Candidates

relatedModels.name: Byte-Level BPE
relatedModels.description: Byte-Level BPE applies BPE over byte representations rather than Unicode characters, allowing a tokenizer to represent arbitrary text and reducing unknown-token problems.

sources.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

relatedModels.name: tiktoken
relatedModels.description: A fast tokenizer implementation used by OpenAI model families, implementing byte-pair encoding and model-specific vocabularies.

relatedModels.name: ByT5
relatedModels.description: ByT5 removes the conventional subword tokenizer and operates directly on UTF-8 bytes, allowing the model to handle arbitrary text and noisy inputs without vocabulary-based tokenization.

sources.title: ByT5: Towards a Token-Free Future with Pre-trained Byte-to-Byte Models

relatedModels.name: CANINE
relatedModels.description: CANINE operates directly on characters rather than subword tokens, using downsampling and Transformer processing to make character-level modeling computationally practical.

sources.title: CANINE: Pre-training an Efficient Tokenization-Free Encoder for Language Representation

relatedModels.name: Charformer
relatedModels.description: Charformer learns latent subword-like representations directly from character sequences using a fast soft tokenization mechanism, avoiding a fixed external tokenizer.

sources.title: Charformer: Fast Character Transformers via Gradient-based Subword Tokenization

relatedModels.name: MegaByte
relatedModels.description: MegaByte performs autoregressive modeling directly over bytes using a multi-scale architecture that separates local byte modeling from longer-range patch modeling.

sources.title: MegaByte: Predicting Million-byte Sequences with Multiscale Transformers

relatedModels.name: Llama SentencePiece Tokenization
relatedModels.description: The Llama family uses a SentencePiece-based subword tokenizer with byte fallback, providing a robust multilingual text representation for decoder-only Transformer models.

relatedModels.name: ViT Patch Embedding
relatedModels.description: Vision Transformer represents an image as a sequence of fixed-size image patches that are projected into token embeddings and processed by a Transformer.

relatedModels.name: VQ-VAE
relatedModels.description: VQ-VAE learns a discrete latent representation using vector quantization, creating a codebook of learned representations that can turn continuous inputs such as images into discrete latent tokens.

relatedModels.name: VQGAN
relatedModels.description: VQGAN combines vector-quantized latent representations with adversarial and perceptual objectives to learn compact high-quality discrete image representations.

sources.title: Taming Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis

relatedModels.name: Vision-Language Projection
relatedModels.description: A learned projection maps visual representations produced by a vision encoder into the representation space expected by a language model, enabling multimodal token sequences.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: visual embeddings projected into language space

relatedModels.name: Audio Tokenization
relatedModels.description: Audio foundation models can represent speech and sound through spectrogram features, learned continuous embeddings, or discrete acoustic tokens produced by neural codecs.

sources.title: SoundStream: An End-to-End Neural Audio Codec

relatedModels.name: EnCodec
relatedModels.description: EnCodec is a neural audio codec that compresses audio into discrete codes, providing a representation that can be modeled by generative architectures.

relatedModels.name: Causal Language Modeling
relatedModels.description: Causal language modeling trains a model to predict the next token from preceding tokens, forming the dominant pretraining objective for decoder-only foundation models.

architecture.family: decoder-only Transformer or compatible sequence model

limitations: Potentially inefficient use of context compared with bidirectional objectives

sources.title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

relatedModels.name: Masked Language Modeling
relatedModels.description: Masked Language Modeling hides selected tokens and trains the model to reconstruct them using surrounding context, enabling bidirectional representation learning.
limitations: Pretraining objective differs from natural generation

sources.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

relatedModels.name: Span Corruption
relatedModels.description: Span corruption masks contiguous spans of input text and trains a sequence-to-sequence model to reconstruct the missing spans, providing a general text-to-text pretraining objective.
limitations: Encoder-decoder inference can be more expensive than decoder-only models for some workloads

sources.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

relatedModels.name: Prefix Language Modeling
relatedModels.description: Prefix language modeling provides bidirectional attention within a prefix while using causal attention for subsequent tokens, combining aspects of encoder-style context understanding with autoregressive generation.
advantages: Strong conditioning on a known prefix

sources.title: Unified Language Model Pre-training for Natural Language Understanding and Generation

relatedModels.name: Contrastive Learning
relatedModels.description: Contrastive learning trains representations by bringing positive examples closer together while separating negative examples in embedding space.
limitations: Negative-sample design can strongly affect training

sources.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations

relatedModels.name: CLIP-Style Image-Text Contrastive Learning
relatedModels.description: CLIP-style training jointly learns image and text representations by maximizing similarity between matching image-text pairs and minimizing similarity between mismatched pairs.
limitations: Performance depends on image-text data quality
Contrastive objective does not directly provide generative behavior

sources.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

relatedModels.name: Supervised Fine-Tuning
relatedModels.description: Supervised fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model using curated input-output examples, often transforming a base model into an instruction-following model.
advantages: Can specialize models for specific domains
limitations: Quality depends heavily on demonstration data
May reduce generality if fine-tuning is narrow

sources.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

relatedModels.name: RLHF
relatedModels.description: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback uses human preference judgments to train a reward model and then optimizes a language model toward preferred behavior.
advantages: Can improve helpfulness and instruction following

sources.title: Learning to Summarize from Human Feedback

relatedModels.name: Proximal Policy Optimization
relatedModels.description: PPO is a policy optimization algorithm that constrains policy updates to maintain stable learning, and became a common optimization method for RLHF pipelines.

relatedModels.name: Direct Preference Optimization
relatedModels.description: DPO directly optimizes a language model from preference pairs without requiring a separately trained reward model or an explicit reinforcement-learning loop.

sources.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model

relatedModels.name: RLAIF
relatedModels.description: RLAIF replaces or supplements human preference labeling with judgments generated by an AI feedback model, allowing preference data to be produced at greater scale.
limitations: AI feedback may amplify model-specific errors

sources.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

relatedModels.name: Group Relative Policy Optimization
relatedModels.description: GRPO is a policy optimization method that estimates relative advantages within groups of sampled responses and avoids requiring a separate value model, making it attractive for reinforcement learning of reasoning models.
advantages: Useful for reasoning tasks with verifiable rewards
limitations: Training dynamics depend strongly on sampling and reward design

sources.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models

relatedModels.name: Rejection Sampling
relatedModels.description: Rejection sampling generates multiple candidate outputs and retains only responses that satisfy a reward model, verifier, or quality criterion for subsequent training.
limitations: Potentially expensive because multiple samples are generated

sources.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

relatedModels.name: Knowledge Distillation
relatedModels.description: Knowledge distillation trains a smaller student model to reproduce information contained in a larger teacher model, transferring behavior or representations while reducing deployment cost.
limitations: Student may fail to reproduce rare capabilities

sources.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network

relatedModels.name: Continued Pretraining
relatedModels.description: Continued pretraining extends the original pretraining process using additional domain-specific, language-specific, temporal, or higher-quality data before supervised or preference-based post-training.

sources.title: Don't Stop Pretraining: Adapt Language Models to Domains and Tasks

relatedModels.name: Synthetic Data Training
relatedModels.description: Synthetic data training uses models, simulators, verifiers, or programmatic processes to generate additional training examples, often targeting specific capabilities or data distributions.
limitations: Distribution quality is difficult to guarantee
Synthetic data can reduce diversity if poorly constructed

sources.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions

relatedModels.name: Constitutional AI
relatedModels.description: Constitutional AI uses explicit principles to critique and revise model responses and can use AI-generated feedback instead of relying exclusively on human preference labels.

training.data: AI-generated critiques, revisions, and preference data

advantages: Reduces dependence on direct human preference labels
limitations: Quality depends on the chosen principles and evaluator
Does not eliminate alignment specification challenges

sources.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

relatedModels.name: Parameter Scaling
relatedModels.description: Parameter scaling studies how increasing the number of learned parameters affects model capability, loss, compute requirements, memory consumption, and downstream performance.
advantages: Can improve performance with sufficient data and compute
limitations: Higher inference cost for dense models
Requires sufficient training data and compute

sources.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

relatedModels.name: Neural Scaling Laws
relatedModels.description: Neural scaling laws describe empirical relationships between model loss and quantities such as model size, dataset size, and compute budget.
advantages: Provides empirical guidance for model design
limitations: Downstream capabilities may not scale identically to pretraining loss

sources.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

relatedModels.name: Chinchilla Compute-Optimal Scaling
relatedModels.description: Chinchilla demonstrated that many large language models were undertrained relative to their parameter count and showed that, under a fixed compute budget, model size and training data should be scaled together.
advantages: Changed how large language models were sized
limitations: Optimal ratios depend on assumptions and regime
Inference economics can favor different parameter/data choices

relatedModels.name: Data Scaling
relatedModels.description: Data scaling studies how increasing the amount, diversity, quality, and repetition characteristics of training data affects foundation-model performance.
advantages: Can improve capability without proportionally increasing parameter count
limitations: High-quality data is difficult to obtain
Data contamination and duplication can distort training

relatedModels.name: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Scaling
relatedModels.description: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts allows total parameter capacity to increase while activating only a subset of experts for each token, reducing the compute growth associated with dense parameter scaling.

scaling.effect: higher parameter capacity at lower per-token computation

advantages: Lower active computation than equivalent dense model

sources.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer

relatedModels.name: Neural Network Quantization
relatedModels.description: Quantization reduces the numerical precision used to represent model weights, activations, or both, reducing memory usage and potentially improving inference efficiency.

scaling.effect: lower memory and potentially faster inference

sources.title: Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only Inference

relatedModels.name: GPTQ
relatedModels.organization: IST Austria / ETH Zurich / Stanford / others
relatedModels.description: GPTQ performs approximate second-order post-training quantization of large language model weights, enabling highly compressed low-bit models without retraining the full network.

sources.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers

relatedModels.name: AWQ
relatedModels.description: Activation-aware Weight Quantization protects salient weight channels identified through activation statistics while quantizing the majority of weights to low precision.

sources.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration

relatedModels.name: Neural Network Pruning
relatedModels.description: Pruning removes weights, neurons, heads, channels, or structured components judged to be unnecessary, reducing model size or computation.
advantages: Can preserve much of the original capability
limitations: Unstructured sparsity may not provide real hardware speedups

sources.title: Learning both Weights and Connections for Efficient Neural Networks

relatedModels.name: KV Cache
relatedModels.description: KV caching stores previously computed key and value representations during autoregressive generation so that they do not need to be recomputed for every newly generated token.

scaling.variable: cached sequence length × KV representation size

advantages: Avoids recomputation of previous K/V states
limitations: Can become the dominant inference-memory cost

sources.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need

relatedModels.name: PagedAttention
relatedModels.description: PagedAttention manages KV-cache memory using non-contiguous blocks inspired by virtual memory systems, improving memory utilization and serving throughput for large language model inference.

sources.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention

relatedModels.name: Speculative Decoding
relatedModels.description: Speculative decoding uses a smaller draft model to propose multiple tokens that are then verified in parallel by a larger target model, potentially increasing generation throughput without changing the target model's output distribution.

sources.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding

relatedModels.name: Medusa
relatedModels.description: Medusa adds multiple decoding heads to a language model so that several future tokens can be predicted simultaneously and verified efficiently during generation.
advantages: Can accelerate decoding without a separate draft model

sources.title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads

relatedModels.name: Data Parallelism
relatedModels.description: Data parallelism replicates a model across devices and assigns different batches of training data to each replica, synchronizing gradients across workers.

scaling.effect: larger effective batch and parallel training

limitations: Each device must hold the model or relevant shard

relatedModels.name: Tensor Parallelism
relatedModels.description: Tensor parallelism partitions individual neural-network operations such as matrix multiplications across multiple devices so that a single layer is computed collaboratively.
advantages: Allows layers larger than one device's memory

sources.title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism

relatedModels.name: Pipeline Parallelism
relatedModels.description: Pipeline parallelism partitions a neural network into sequential stages placed on different devices and processes multiple microbatches concurrently through the pipeline.
advantages: Allows very large models to span devices

sources.title: PipeDream: Generalized Pipeline Parallelism for DNN Training

relatedModels.name: ZeRO
relatedModels.description: ZeRO partitions optimizer states, gradients, and optionally model parameters across data-parallel workers, substantially reducing redundant memory consumption.

sources.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models

relatedModels.name: Expert Parallelism
relatedModels.description: Expert parallelism distributes different Mixture-of-Experts expert networks across devices and routes tokens between devices according to the gating decisions.

relatedModels.name: Recurrent Neural Network
relatedModels.description: Recurrent Neural Networks process sequences sequentially while maintaining a hidden state that carries information from previous positions.
advantages: Low memory footprint relative to full attention

relatedModels.name: Long Short-Term Memory
relatedModels.description: LSTM introduces gated memory cells that control information flow into, out of, and within a recurrent state, improving the ability to preserve information over long sequences.
advantages: Improved long-range memory over vanilla RNNs
Useful for sequential and streaming tasks
limitations: Less scalable for very large foundation models

relatedModels.name: Gated Recurrent Unit
relatedModels.description: GRU is a gated recurrent architecture that simplifies LSTM-style memory using update and reset gates.
advantages: Lower parameter count than many LSTM configurations
limitations: Limited scalability compared with highly parallel architectures

sources.title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation

relatedModels.name: State Space Model
relatedModels.description: State Space Models represent sequence dynamics through a latent state that evolves as inputs arrive, providing an alternative to explicit pairwise attention for long sequences.
advantages: Linear-time sequence processing in relevant formulations
limitations: Different optimization and representation tradeoffs from attention
State compression can limit direct access to all previous tokens

sources.title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces

relatedModels.name: S4
relatedModels.description: S4 uses structured state space representations designed to efficiently model long-range dependencies while maintaining computationally efficient sequence processing.
limitations: Less widely deployed than Transformer architectures

sources.title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces

relatedModels.name: S5
relatedModels.description: S5 simplifies multi-input multi-output state space modeling by using a single state space layer, reducing some of the complexity of earlier structured state space approaches.
advantages: Simpler architecture than some S4 formulations
limitations: Still less established than Transformer architectures

sources.title: Simplified State Space Layers for Sequence Modeling

relatedModels.name: Mamba
relatedModels.description: Mamba introduces selective state space modeling in which input-dependent parameters control what information is propagated through the recurrent state, providing a linear-scaling alternative to attention for sequence modeling.
limitations: Does not provide direct pairwise token-to-token attention
Capability tradeoffs vary by task and model design
Architecture and kernels are more specialized

sources.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

relatedModels.name: Mamba-2
relatedModels.description: Mamba-2 develops a structured state space approach that connects state space modeling and attention-like computation while improving hardware efficiency and simplifying the underlying formulation.

memory.complexity: linear-time sequence processing in the core formulation

limitations: Tradeoffs versus attention depend on workload

sources.title: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality

relatedModels.name: Mamba-3
relatedModels.description: Mamba-3 represents the subsequent evolution of the Mamba family, exploring improved state-space formulations and training mechanisms for language and long-context modeling.

relatedModels.name: RWKV
relatedModels.description: RWKV combines recurrent-style sequence processing with attention-inspired weighting, enabling efficient inference with constant-size recurrent state while retaining Transformer-like training characteristics.
limitations: Different scaling and capability tradeoffs from mainstream Transformers

sources.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era

relatedModels.name: RetNet
relatedModels.description: RetNet introduces a retention mechanism designed to provide parallelizable training, recurrent inference, and efficient sequence computation as alternatives to standard Transformer attention.
limitations: Tradeoffs depend on task and implementation

sources.title: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models

relatedModels.name: Hyena
relatedModels.description: Hyena replaces explicit quadratic attention with long convolutions and element-wise gating, providing a subquadratic alternative for long-context sequence modeling.

sources.title: Hyena Hierarchy: Towards Larger Convolutional Language Models

relatedModels.name: Linear Attention
relatedModels.description: Linear attention reformulates attention computation so that the sequence-length dependence can be reduced from quadratic to linear under specific kernel or feature-map formulations.

memory.complexity: linear in sequence length under applicable formulations

limitations: Approximation or reformulation can alter attention behavior

sources.title: Transformers are RNNs: Fast Autoregressive Transformers with Linear Attention

relatedModels.name: xLSTM
relatedModels.description: xLSTM revisits recurrent memory using exponential gating and new scalar and matrix memory variants designed to improve scalability and long-range sequence modeling.
limitations: Deployment and scaling evidence is smaller than Transformer ecosystem

relatedModels.name: Hybrid Attention-State Space Architecture
relatedModels.description: Hybrid architectures combine attention layers with state-space or recurrent layers, attempting to capture both direct token-to-token interactions and efficient long-range state propagation.
advantages: Can reduce dependence on full attention

relatedModels.name: Jamba
relatedModels.description: Jamba combines Transformer attention, Mamba-style state space layers, and Mixture-of-Experts components in a hybrid architecture designed for efficient long-context language modeling.

relatedModels.name: Dual-Encoder Multimodal Architecture
relatedModels.description: A dual-encoder architecture independently encodes two modalities into compatible representation spaces and aligns them using a similarity or contrastive objective.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: independent encoding followed by representation alignment

sources.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

relatedModels.name: CLIP
relatedModels.description: CLIP jointly trains an image encoder and a text encoder to produce aligned representations using large-scale image-text contrastive learning.
limitations: Not a general-purpose multimodal conversational model

sources.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

relatedModels.name: SigLIP
relatedModels.description: SigLIP is a vision-language dual encoder that replaces CLIP's softmax contrastive objective with a pairwise sigmoid loss for image-text alignment.
advantages: Useful as a vision encoder for multimodal models
limitations: Not inherently a general-purpose conversational generator

sources.title: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training

relatedModels.name: Cross-Attention Multimodal Fusion
relatedModels.description: Cross-attention fusion allows representations from one modality to attend to representations from another modality, enabling token-level or feature-level multimodal interaction.

fusion.mechanism: queries from one modality attend to keys and values from another

limitations: Cross-attention memory grows with multimodal sequence sizes

relatedModels.name: Flamingo
relatedModels.description: Flamingo connects a pretrained vision encoder to a pretrained language model through specialized cross-attention layers, enabling few-shot multimodal generation.
advantages: Supports interleaved visual and textual inputs

sources.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning

relatedModels.name: BLIP-2
relatedModels.description: BLIP-2 connects frozen vision and language models through a lightweight Querying Transformer that learns to extract visual information useful for language generation.
advantages: Efficient reuse of frozen pretrained components
Strong visual question answering and image understanding
limitations: Depends on quality of pretrained components

sources.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models

relatedModels.name: Vision-Language Projection
relatedModels.description: A modality projector maps representations produced by a vision encoder into the representation space expected by a language model.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: visual tokens projected into language-model space

advantages: Easy integration with pretrained language models
limitations: Projection can create an information bottleneck

relatedModels.name: LLaVA
relatedModels.organization: University of Wisconsin–Madison / Microsoft Research / Columbia University
relatedModels.description: LLaVA connects a pretrained vision encoder to a large language model through a learned projection layer, enabling visual instruction following and multimodal conversation.

architecture.sequenceStrategy: visual tokens inserted into language sequence

advantages: Easy adaptation of existing language models
limitations: Vision information must pass through a projector
Performance depends on vision encoder and language model

relatedModels.name: PaliGemma
relatedModels.description: PaliGemma combines a SigLIP vision encoder with a Gemma language model in a compact vision-language architecture designed for image understanding and generation tasks.
limitations: Architecture has a relatively constrained multimodal interface
Capability depends on model scale and adaptation

relatedModels.name: Qwen-VL
relatedModels.description: Qwen-VL integrates visual representations with the Qwen language-model family to support image understanding, visual question answering, and multimodal generation.
limitations: Exact components should be recorded per release

sources.title: Qwen-VL: A Versatile Vision-Language Model for Understanding, Localization, Text Reading, and Beyond

relatedModels.name: InternVL
relatedModels.description: InternVL is a vision-language model family that combines large-scale visual encoders with language models and progressively improves visual understanding, resolution handling, and multimodal instruction following.
limitations: High-resolution processing can increase computational cost

sources.title: InternVL: Scaling up Vision Foundation Models and Aligning for Generic Visual-Linguistic Tasks

relatedModels.name: IDEFICS
relatedModels.description: IDEFICS is an open vision-language model family designed for image-text understanding and generation using pretrained vision and language components.
limitations: Earlier generation compared with newer VLMs
Performance varies significantly by model version

sources.title: IDEFICS: An Open Reproduction of Flamingo

relatedModels.name: KOSMOS
relatedModels.description: KOSMOS explores a general multimodal language modeling framework capable of grounding language in visual information and supporting tasks such as image understanding and multimodal interaction.

fusion.mechanism: visual embeddings integrated into language sequence

advantages: Grounding of language in visual context
limitations: Earlier architecture relative to current VLM systems

sources.title: Language Is Not All You Need: Aligning Perception with Language Models

relatedModels.name: Early Multimodal Token Fusion
relatedModels.description: Early multimodal fusion represents multiple modalities as tokens or token-like representations that can be processed jointly by a shared autoregressive Transformer.

relatedModels.name: Chameleon
relatedModels.description: Chameleon is a mixed-modal early-fusion foundation model that processes interleaved text and image tokens within a shared autoregressive Transformer framework.

relatedModels.name: Janus
relatedModels.description: Janus explores unified multimodal understanding and generation while decoupling visual encoding strategies for the two tasks, allowing the system to handle both perception and image generation.

architecture.family: unified multimodal model with decoupled visual pathways
architecture.sequenceStrategy: unified language modeling with decoupled visual encoding

advantages: Combines multimodal understanding and image generation
Explores unified architecture with task-specific visual representations

sources.title: Janus: Decoupling Visual Encoding for Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation

relatedModels.name: Word-Level Tokenization
relatedModels.description: Word-level tokenization represents text primarily as complete words or whitespace-delimited units. It is conceptually simple but produces very large vocabularies and struggles with rare, unseen, and morphologically complex words.

efficiency.sequenceLength: shorter than subword tokenization for many texts

relatedModels.name: Character-Level Representation
relatedModels.description: Character-level representation treats individual characters as the basic sequence units, avoiding vocabulary-level unknown words at the cost of much longer sequences.

representation.unknownToken: often unnecessary for known character sets

efficiency.memory: low vocabulary cost but high sequence-processing cost

advantages: Handles arbitrary words through character composition
limitations: Higher computational cost for long text

relatedModels.name: Byte Pair Encoding
relatedModels.description: Byte Pair Encoding builds a subword vocabulary by iteratively merging frequently occurring symbol pairs. In neural language modeling it provides a compromise between character-level flexibility and word-level efficiency.
advantages: Balances vocabulary size and sequence length
limitations: Can be inefficient for some languages and domains

sources.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

relatedModels.name: WordPiece
relatedModels.description: WordPiece represents text using a learned vocabulary of subword units and was widely used in Transformer encoder models such as BERT.
advantages: Handles unknown and rare words better than word-level tokenization
Effective for multilingual and general NLP settings
limitations: Can produce inefficient sequences for some languages

relatedModels.name: SentencePiece
relatedModels.description: SentencePiece is a language-independent tokenization framework that learns subword segmentation directly from raw text without requiring whitespace-based preprocessing.
limitations: Tokenizer behavior depends on training configuration
Segmentation can differ substantially across model families

sources.title: SentencePiece: A simple and language independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer for Neural Text Processing

relatedModels.name: Unigram Language Model Tokenization
relatedModels.description: Unigram tokenization starts from a large candidate vocabulary and iteratively removes pieces according to a probabilistic language-model objective, selecting segmentations based on likelihood.
advantages: Multiple possible segmentations can be modeled

sources.title: Subword Regularization: Improving Neural Network Translation Models with Multiple Subword Candidates

relatedModels.name: Byte-Level BPE
relatedModels.description: Byte-level BPE applies BPE-style merging over byte representations, allowing arbitrary text and Unicode content to be represented without relying on a fixed character vocabulary.

representation.unknownToken: typically unnecessary for arbitrary byte sequences

advantages: Works across languages and unusual strings
limitations: Some languages can require many tokens
Token efficiency depends strongly on vocabulary and corpus

sources.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

relatedModels.name: Byte-Level Representation
relatedModels.description: Byte-level representation processes raw byte sequences directly or with minimal learned segmentation, providing universal coverage of textual data while potentially increasing sequence length.

efficiency.memory: low vocabulary cost but potentially high sequence-processing cost

relatedModels.name: Vision Patch Tokenization
relatedModels.description: Vision patch tokenization divides an image into fixed-size or structured patches and maps each patch to an embedding that can be processed as a sequence of visual tokens.

efficiency.sequenceLength: proportional to image area and inverse patch area

advantages: Simple conversion of images into Transformer-compatible sequences
limitations: Fixed patch size may lose fine-grained information

sources.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale

relatedModels.name: Discrete Image Tokenization
relatedModels.description: Discrete image tokenization converts continuous visual information into a sequence of discrete codebook indices, allowing image content to be modeled using token-prediction architectures.
advantages: Allows image generation using token prediction

relatedModels.name: Audio Tokenization
relatedModels.description: Audio tokenization converts speech, music, or general audio into compact continuous or discrete representations that can be processed by sequence models.

representation.unit: audio frame or discrete codec code

efficiency.sequenceLength: depends on frame rate and compression

advantages: Can support speech generation and understanding
limitations: Temporal sequences can remain very long

relatedModels.name: EnCodec
relatedModels.description: EnCodec is a neural audio codec that compresses audio into discrete latent representations using an encoder, quantization mechanism, and decoder.
advantages: Discrete representations suitable for generative modeling
limitations: Multiple codebooks can increase sequence complexity

relatedModels.name: Speech Tokenization
relatedModels.description: Speech tokenization represents spoken language as learned acoustic, phonetic, semantic, or codec units that can be modeled by sequence architectures.
advantages: Allows speech to be modeled as discrete sequences
Can unify speech and language modeling
limitations: Speech contains information at multiple timescales

relatedModels.name: Video Tokenization
relatedModels.description: Video tokenization converts spatial and temporal visual information into sequences of visual tokens representing frames, patches, or compressed spatiotemporal units.

efficiency.sequenceLength: grows with spatial and temporal resolution

relatedModels.name: Unified Multimodal Token Space
relatedModels.description: A unified multimodal token space represents multiple modalities using compatible token-like representations that can be processed within a common sequence-modeling framework.

efficiency.memory: depends on total multimodal token count

limitations: Token counts can become extremely large
Different modalities have very different information densities

relatedModels.name: Tokenizer-Free Modeling
relatedModels.description: Tokenizer-free models process byte-level or character-level representations directly rather than relying on a conventional learned subword tokenizer, aiming to simplify multilingual and arbitrary-text processing.

efficiency.memory: low vocabulary cost but potentially higher sequence-processing cost

advantages: Potentially better handling of unusual strings
limitations: Higher compute requirements for equivalent text
Requires architectures optimized for long sequences

sources.title: ByT5: Towards a Token-Free Future with Pre-trained Byte-to-Byte Models

relatedModels.name: ByT5
relatedModels.description: ByT5 is a tokenizer-free sequence-to-sequence Transformer that operates directly on UTF-8 byte sequences rather than conventional subword tokens.

sources.title: ByT5: Towards a Token-Free Future with Pre-trained Byte-to-Byte Models
